candidateSQLite.interpretation: Finite overloaded completion plateau around 2.27-2.35k/s in final 10 seconds; all 30 seconds reject at both high rates. Not a maximum loss-free capacity.

candidatePostgresql.interpretation: Final10 completion rates around 2.70-2.74k/s with rejection every second. The 3600 cell is nonstationary across its three 10-second blocks (2216.3,2213.5,2738.8/s); do not call whole-window 2389.9/s exact capacity.

findings.dapperHighestCells: SQLite4000 final10 3992.4/s with 2 rejection seconds; PG4800 final10 4770.4/s with 3 rejection seconds. Still largely follows offered rate; no sustained plateau located.
findings.firstRefusalInterpretation: First tested rate with any refusal, not a precise monotonic or sustainable-capacity threshold.

localRepeatRecommendations.question: Locate Dapper sustained overload rather than treating transient refusal as saturation.
localRepeatRecommendations.suggestion: Use a new explicit local plan with one higher cell per provider (for example SQLite6000/s and PG7200/s, queue64 and current workers). If still tracking offered rate, extend one step; repeat the first adjacent high-rate pair that shows dense continuing rejections and a completion plateau. Do not extrapolate capacity from current top cells.

localRepeatRecommendations.question: Test the non-monotonic low-rate refusal observation.
localRepeatRecommendations.suggestion: A reversed PG Dapper2400/1200 pair is the clearest small repeat: current1200 rejects at seconds8/10/17 but2400 rejects zero. If strict zero-refusal-envelope decisions depend on SQLite, repeat its Dapper4000/2000 pair; do not rerun all16 cells.

localRepeatRecommendations.question: Resolve the PG candidate3600 transient before assigning a plateau.
localRepeatRecommendations.suggestion: One reversed candidate4800/3600 pair with a somewhat longer separately identified duration (for example60s) and the same fixed final10-second summary can distinguish the 3600 early/mid slowdown from a stable tail. The existing SQLite high cells already show rejection every second; no broad repeat is needed merely to demonstrate their overload.

limitations: Each rate/variant has one serial 30-second window; offered rate rises within provider and route order alternates. This is not a replicated capacity curve or a confidence interval.

Whole-window success throughput uses actual start-through-drain elapsed time. Last10Seconds uses completed operations timestamped in [20,30), excludes drain seconds, and is not a cohort of requests admitted only in that interval.
Last 10 seconds are a fixed descriptive subsection, not a proof of stationarity. First/middle/final 10-second rates, per-second min/max/CV and slope are retained to reveal transients.
Per-second Planned is due-time schedule. Sent/Rejected and completions use actual event times. Do not force Planned=Sent+Rejected in each bucket; full-series ledgers close exactly.
Rejected work is admission rejection, not a business error. Service/scheduled latency histograms cover accepted successful work and exclude rejected requests.

Process CPU includes the spinning arrival producer, failed admission work, harness, drivers/framework and business materialization. Ratios cannot isolate execution paths or be corrected by subtracting an assumed producer budget.
Native allocation and framework-only managed bytes are unknown. Peak RSS is through a measurement snapshot; released RSS follows tracked-owner release and five seconds idle without forced GC.
PG sampled inner/outer visible-proc CPU is non-atomic observation, not an exact steady bound. Separate wait4 lifetime includes initialization/warmup/idle/shutdown and is never added to sampled CPU.

Every business case succeeds and matches its oracle, but admission rejection changes accepted case counts; exact35-class success shares and deviations from uniform are retained. A changed mix or selective dropping of more/less allocating business must not be called a framework allocation improvement. Per-class rejection causes or counterfactual costs are not inferred.
Physical PG fixtures retired by the root were not read or recreated. All analysis uses retained raw/config/validation/controller evidence.
